title: 2008 AMC 10A Problem 24
statement: Let \(k = 2008^2 + 2^{2008}.\) What is the units digit of \(k^2 + 2^k?\)

solutions.text:
The units digit of \(2^n\) cycles \(2, 4, 8, 6,\) so \(2^{2008}\) ends in \(6.\) Also \(2008^2\) ends in \(4.\)

Thus \(k\) ends in \(0,\) so \(k^2\) ends in \(0.\)

Both \(2008^2\) and \(2^{2008}\) are multiples of \(4,\) so \(k \equiv 0 \pmod 4,\) which makes \(2^k\) end in \(6.\)

The units digit of \(k^2 + 2^k\) is \(0 + 6 = 6.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Find the units digit of \(k\) first
\(2^{2008}\) ends in \(6\) and \(2008^2\) ends in \(4;\) then determine \(k \bmod 4\) to handle \(2^k\)
